screens.title: Which deletion hurts?
screens.text: Both 10 and 50 are leaves. Which deletion makes the tree unbalanced?
screens.reveal: Deleting 10 leaves node 20 with an empty left branch and a right branch of height 1: bf = 1 − (−1) = +2.

screens.title: Goal
screens.text: Delete a leaf from an AVL tree and restore the AVL property (LO7). This app covers leaf deletion only. Deleting a node with children (delete by copying) is covered in the lecture.

task.stem: How do you delete a leaf from a BST?
task.hint: This checks leaf deletion: a leaf is simply removed; no other node moves until balance is checked.

options.explanation: The parent stays where it is. Only the leaf is removed.

options.text: Move its sibling into its place
options.explanation: The sibling stays where it is. Only the leaf is removed.

options.text: Remove it: its parent’s branch becomes empty

screens.title: Deleting 50: no rotation needed
screens.text: Remove the leaf, then update balance factors from its parent up to the root.
steps: Every node has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1.

screens.title: Deleting 10: one rotation
screens.caption: Node 20 has bf +2 and its right child 40 has bf 0: a single left rotation about 20.
steps: Node 20 has balance factor +2: it is unbalanced.
Every node has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1.

screens.title: Leaf deletion
points: 2. Update balance factors from its parent up to the root.
3. If a node has bf +2 and its right child has bf 0 or +1: single left rotation about that node.
4. If a node has bf −2 and its left child has bf 0 or −1: single right rotation about that node.
If the child leans the other way, a double rotation is needed. The examples in this app avoid that case; the lecture covers it.
screens.showRule: Remove the leaf, update bf up to the root, rotate towards the shorter branch.

screens.title: Worked example: the mirror case
screens.caption: Node 30 has bf −2 and its left child 20 has bf 0: a single right rotation about 30.
steps: Node 30 has balance factor −2: it is unbalanced.
Every node has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1.

task.stem: Delete 30 and rebalance. Build the final tree.
task.hint: This checks rebalancing after a deletion: at the unbalanced node, a single rotation towards the shorter branch restores balance.

feedback.correct: After removing 30, node 50 has bf +2 and its right child 70 has bf +1: a single left rotation about 50 gives 70(50, 80).
feedback.incorrect: After removing 30, node 50 has bf +2 and its right child 70 has bf +1: a single left rotation about 50 gives 70(50, 80).

task.stem: 80 has just been deleted. Enter the new balance factors of 70 and 50.
task.hint: This checks that you can update balance factors after a deletion: start at the removed leaf’s parent and work up to the root.

wrongAnswers.feedback: The sign is reversed. The balance factor is the height of the right branch minus the height of the left branch. Node 50: its right branch has height 0 and its left branch has height 1, so bf = 0 − 1 = −1. A taller left branch gives a negative number.
That is node 50’s balance factor before the deletion. After removing a leaf, update every node on the path up to the root.

feedback.correct: Node 70: its right branch is empty (height −1) and its left branch is empty (height −1), so bf = −1 − (−1) = 0. Node 50: its right branch has height 0 and its left branch has height 1, so bf = 0 − 1 = −1.
feedback.incorrect: Node 70: its right branch is empty (height −1) and its left branch is empty (height −1), so bf = −1 − (−1) = 0. Node 50: its right branch has height 0 and its left branch has height 1, so bf = 0 − 1 = −1.

screens.title: Lesson check
screens.text: One question for each assessment criterion of this lesson’s objective. Each question allows one re-attempt, and the hint is always available.

screens.title: Summary
points: A leaf is simply removed; nothing else moves.
Update balance factors from the parent up to the root.
At a node with bf ±2, rotate towards the shorter branch.
